lines.text: Do you know how an eSIM works, with no card at all?
For years, your number lived on a tiny plastic card. Lose it, snap it, and you're stuck.
An eSIM is a chip soldered right onto your phone's board. Nothing to pop out.
Your carrier sends it a profile. A little locked package with your number and your keys, downloaded over the internet.
Usually you just scan a QR code. It tells your phone where to fetch the profile, and gives it a code to claim it.
One chip can hold several profiles. Home number, travel number. Switch with a tap.
Orbi Transfer uses the same trick. Every file gets its own QR code and a short code, so another phone can grab it in seconds.
